title: Role ramp backstop and probation checklist playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This playbook is a pragmatic, manager-facing tool for two related problems we keep hitting: 1) ad-hoc role ramps that drift past expected timelines, and 2) lack of a clear backstop/escalation when probation signals are negative. It is intended for People Ops partners and hiring/managing managers for IC and manager hires across teams (eng, product, go-to-market).

High-level goals:
- Reduce variance in time-to-autonomy for new hires by codifying a 30/60/90 ramp plus backstop triggers.
- Provide a short, repeatable escalation path when new hire outcomes don't match expectations.
- Surface hiring/prioritization signals so hiring managers and recruiting agree on acceptance thresholds up front.

Quick definitions (team shorthand):
- Ramp signal: quantitative/qualitative evidence that someone is progressing (code reviews merged, feature ownership, stakeholder check-ins).
- Backstop: an agreed set of interventions (mentoring shift, role narrowing, performance plan, or off-ramp) that are enacted when signals are negative.
- Probation period: first 90 calendar days after start unless otherwise negotiated.

Part A: Hiring priority triage (pre-offer)
1) Role readiness checklist (completed at offer):
   - Hiring manager checklist: must attach at offer: 1) three prioritized 90-day outcomes (must be measurable), 2) list of required stakeholders and owners for onboarding, 3) primary mentor assigned.
   - Recruiter checklist: confirm candidate acceptance includes start date, timezone constraints, and required compliances (NDAs, vetting).
2) Acceptance thresholds (minimums for offers):
   - Strong hire: scored >= 8 on final rubric and has explicit examples for 2 of 3 priority outcomes.
   - Conditional hire: scored 6–7 and hiring manager commits to a 15-day focused mentor plan (documented).
   - Reject: score <=5 or critical skill gaps without feasible remediation.
3) Priority signal tags (used in ATS): must tag new hire with at least one: "fast-ramp", "needs-mentor", "high-uncertainty". These bubble up to People Ops for resource planning.

Part B: 30/60/90 ramp checklist (manager + People Ops joint)
Template outcomes (manager fills): objective, measurable, and owner-aligned. Example: "Ship data schema validation MVP and own production rollout checklist by day 60."

30-day: foundation
- Orientation completed: company systems, security training, payroll, and access to repos.
- First-week 1:1 cadence with manager scheduled and documented in calendar.
- Mentor onboarding: mentor has a 4-item shadow plan and first week pairing sessions scheduled.
- Quick wins: new hire completes one documented, merged PR or customer-facing doc.
- Manager notes: weekly short feedback posted in private onboarding doc.

60-day: competence
- Primary 90-day outcomes have initial progress evidence (PRs, design notes, stakeholder emails).
- Ownership: candidate has at least one area with read/write permissions and a list of next steps they are responsible for.
- Cross-team sync: introduced to key stakeholders and added to recurring meetings.
- Feedback loop: formal 60-day check-in scheduled and invites include People Ops.

90-day: autonomy check
- Outcomes verification: compare filled outcomes against expected acceptance thresholds.
- Transition plan: if continuing, assign long-term goals and next performance milestones.
- Close-out: People Ops confirms completion of checklist and files final onboarding note to hire record.

Part C: Backstop triggers and remediation options (what to do when signals are negative)
Signals that trigger an escalation (any of these):
- Misses 2+ core milestone deadlines (30/60/90 outcomes) without acceptable blocker documentation.
- Persistent lack of engagement in paired-learning or asynchronous deliverables.
- Repeated feedback from 2+ stakeholders citing quality or collaboration concerns.

Immediate next steps (day 0–3 after trigger):
- Manager documents specific examples in the private performance packet (date+links).
- Rapid sync: People Ops, manager, and mentor meet within 3 business days to triage and decide intervention.

Intervention tiers:
- Tier 1: Mentor intensification (2-week focused pairing + explicit micro-goals). Manager documents daily pairing notes.
- Tier 2: Role narrowing (reduce scope to 1–2 deliverables for 30 days) + weekly status reports to People Ops.
- Tier 3: Formal performance plan (PIP-lite) for 30 days with clear exit criteria; legal/HR loop-in and optional coach assigned.
- Tier 4: Off-ramp discussion (if other tiers fail and evidence supports). People Ops to run off-ramp checklist and closure comms.

Part D: Manager guidance and templates
Manager 60-day check-in script (short bullets):
- Start with strengths observed (2 mins).
- Review 60-day progress against 3 outcomes (5 mins).
- Identify blockers and agreement on 2 concrete next steps (5 mins).
- Ask: "What support would help you be more effective?" (2 mins).
- Close with follow-up: date+owner for next check-in and note saved to onboarding doc (1 min).

Manager note template (to paste in private doc):
- Week X note: date, what went well (bullets), concerns (bullets), objective evidence (links), next steps (owner+date).

Offer acceptance + start-day checklist (concise):
- Confirm start date, timezone, laptop/hardware needs, security email set up, and 1st week meeting schedule sent.
- Slack intro message template: "Hi team — excited to join! I’m X, joining as Y. My focus first 30 days will be X. Please say hi and share any quick tips."

Part E: Interview rubric addendum (use at final onsite/hiring loop)
We keep the main rubric in ATS. Addendum fields to capture ramp signals at hire:
- Evidence of autonomous delivery under ambiguity (1–5).
- Learning velocity (ability to pick up new stack) (1–5).
- Cross-team communication and stakeholder management (1–5).
- Manager’s ramp confidence (1–5, free text comment required).
Scoring guidance: treat combined score >=14 as strong hire, 11–13 conditional, <=10 not ready.

Part F: Documentation and data capture (for people ops metrics)
Required artifacts to attach to the hire packet on day 0: offer letter, manager 90-day outcomes doc, mentor assignment, signed compliance docs.
People Ops metrics to track per hire (minimum): time-to-first-merge, time-to-own-component, 30/60/90 qualitative score, escalation events (Y/N), final outcome (retained/transitioned/off-ramp) — these feed quarterly hiring retrospective.

Open questions / tensions (for discussion):
- Should probation period be 120 days for some specialized roles? Suggested approach: manager flags in role-readiness brief and People Ops approves.
- How do we budget mentor time across many conditional hires? Proposed experiment: central mentor pool with 0.2 FTE allocation for qualifying hires.

Appendix: quick templates and links
- 60-day check-in calendar invite subject: "60-day sync: [New Hire] — progress & blockers"
- People Ops escalation Slack channel: #people-ops-escalations (tag @peopleops-oncall)
- Confluence onboarding folder: /display/HR/Onboarding-Playbooks (please attach final packet here)

Notes to self / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Create an ATS tag map to surface "conditional hire" + mentor assignment automatically (open ticket HIRE-412).
- Draft an email template for off-ramp closure with legal and manager wording (assign to Marco).
- Run a 6-week pilot with two eng teams to validate time-to-autonomy metrics and mentor pool demand.

Acknowledgements: thanks to Sara & Marco for early drafts and Evan for pilot metric suggestions.

End of document.
